items.title: Booking Platform
items.description: Booking system for a chain of climbing gyms, built with Laravel and Vue.js: classes, courses and day passes, waiting lists, card payments and a dashboard for each gym.

study.tagline: A booking system for a chain of climbing gyms: classes, courses and day passes, with payments and a dashboard for each gym.

numbers.label: for a booking at peak time

problem.title: Full classes, empty slots
paragraphs: Each gym took bookings by phone and spreadsheet. Popular classes were overbooked, cancellations left empty slots nobody heard about, and head office had no view across the gyms.

I built the booking platform that replaced it: one system for all gyms, with online booking, waiting lists and payments, and a dashboard for each gym and for head office. This project is fictional demo content.

built.title: Booking and waiting lists
built.text: Members book classes, courses and day passes online. A freed slot goes to the first person on the waiting list, who is told by email.

built.title: Payments
built.text: Card payments and memberships, with refunds when a class is cancelled.

built.title: Dashboards
built.text: Each gym sees its own bookings and capacity. Head office sees every gym side by side.

built.title: Public API
built.text: A REST API for the gyms' own websites and a member app, with documentation.

flow.title: How a booking is made
flow.note: A slot is reserved in a single database transaction, so two people can never book the last place.

hard.title: The last place in a class
hard.text: At peak times dozens of people book the same class at once. Slots are reserved with a row lock in one transaction, so a class can't be overbooked.

hard.title: Moving fourteen gyms over
hard.text: Each gym moved over separately, with its members and memberships imported and checked, while the old process kept running.

items.title: Warehouse Dashboard
items.description: Live dashboard for a warehouse team, built with Symfony: open orders, late shipments and staff load, refreshed every minute, with alerts and weekly reports.

study.tagline: A dashboard that shows a warehouse team what is late, what is waiting and where the day is going, refreshed every minute.

problem.title: Reports that arrived too late
paragraphs: The warehouse team got a daily report the next morning, after the problems it described had already happened.
I built a dashboard that reads the warehouse database every minute and shows open orders, late shipments and staff load as they change. This project is fictional demo content.

built.title: Live overview
built.text: Open orders, late shipments and the day's progress, refreshed every minute.

built.title: Alerts
built.text: An email when an order is at risk of missing its pick-up time.

built.title: Reports
built.text: Weekly summaries as CSV and PDF, for the team and for management.

built.title: Roles
built.text: Team leads, staff and management each see what they need.

flow.title: Where the numbers come from

lanes.title: Database
items: One row per hour and area

flow.note: The dashboard never writes to the warehouse system, so it can't slow down the work on the floor.

hard.title: Fast without touching the source
hard.text: The import reads only what changed since its last run, and keeps hourly totals, so charts load quickly without loading the warehouse database.

hard.title: Alerts people trust
hard.text: An alert is sent once, when an order becomes at risk, and not again until something changes.
